name: Knee Push-Up
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Walk knees back until your body is a straight line from knees to head.
Lower your chest toward the floor with elbows about 45° from your body.
Press back up without letting your hips sag.
tip: Move to full push-ups once you can do 3 × 15 with good form.

name: Push-Up
steps: Hands under shoulders, feet together or slightly apart, body in one straight line.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Lower until your chest is a fist-width from the floor.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tip: Keep your neck neutral by looking at a spot just ahead of your hands.

name: Hand-Release Push-Up
steps: Start in a push-up position.
Lower your chest all the way to the floor.
Lift your hands off the floor for a moment.
Place them back and push up to the top.
tip: The pause on the floor removes momentum and builds strength from the bottom.

name: Diamond Push-Up
steps: Make a diamond with your thumbs and index fingers under your chest.
Keep elbows close to your ribs as you lower.
Press back up to straight arms.
tip: Drop to your knees if your elbows or wrists complain.

name: Air Squat
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, chest up.
Lower until thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as far as is comfortable.
Drive through your whole foot to stand.
tip: Keep your knees tracking over your toes and heels on the floor.

name: Forward Lunge
steps: Stand tall with hands on hips.
Step forward and lower until both knees are bent about 90°.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Alternate legs.
tip: Take a long enough step that your front knee stays above your ankle.

name: Walking Lunge
steps: Take a long step forward and lower into a lunge.
Push off and bring the back foot forward into the next step.
Keep walking in a line, chest tall.
tip: Use a hallway or clear a path of about 4–5 meters.

name: Sit-Up
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Curl your torso up until your elbows reach your thighs.
Lower under control.
tip: If your neck or lower back is sensitive, do a crunch (lift only your shoulder blades) instead.

name: Flutter Kicks
steps: Lie on your back with legs straight and hands under your hips.
Lift your heels a few inches off the floor and lift your head slightly.
Kick your legs up and down in small, quick alternating motions.
tip: Press your lower back into the floor. Raise the legs higher to make it easier on the back.

name: Mountain Climbers
steps: Start in a high plank, hands under shoulders.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs quickly.
Keep your hips low and your core braced.
tip: Slow it down to make it easier.

name: Front Plank
steps: Place forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders.
Extend legs behind you, forming a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes. Breathe steadily.
tip: Stop when your hips sag or your lower back aches.

name: Burpee
steps: Stand, then squat and place hands on the floor.
Jump or step your feet back into a plank.
Do a push-up (optional), then jump or step your feet back in.
Stand and jump up with arms overhead.
tip: Step instead of jumping for a lower-impact version.

name: Eight-Count Bodybuilder
steps: Squat and place hands down. Kick feet back to plank.
Do a push-up. Open feet wide, then bring them together.
Jump or step feet forward, then stand and jump with arms overhead.
tip: Move at a steady pace and keep the push-up strict.

name: Bear Crawl
steps: Start on hands and knees, then lift your knees an inch off the floor.
Crawl forward with opposite hand and foot moving together.
Keep your back flat and hips level.
tip: Crawl back and forth in a clear room.

name: V-Up
steps: Lie flat with arms overhead and legs straight.
At the same time, lift your legs and torso, reaching hands toward toes.
Lower with control.
tip: Bend your knees slightly to make it easier.

name: Deep Core Release Breathing
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, or sit comfortably.
Place one hand on your belly and one on your ribs.
Inhale slowly through your nose and let your belly and pelvic floor soften and drop.
Exhale gently and let everything return.
tip: A pelvic floor that can relax is as important as one that can tighten. This pairs well with every Foundation routine.

name: Brace Before You Cough
dose: Practice 5 times, then use in daily life
steps: Stand or sit upright.
Before you cough, sneeze or lift something, gently lift and tighten your pelvic floor.
Hold the lift through the cough, then release.
tip: This is a protective habit. It trains the muscles to switch on when pressure rises.

name: Foundation Lift Basics (Men)
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Tighten the muscles you would use to stop passing gas. You should feel a gentle lift deep inside, below your belly.
Hold 3 seconds, then fully relax for 3 seconds.
Do not squeeze your buttocks, thighs or abs, and keep breathing.
tip: Don't practice these while urinating. If you feel pain or can't find the muscle, a pelvic floor physiotherapist can help.

name: Foundation Endurance Holds (Men)
dose: 10 reps: hold 5–10 seconds, rest equal time
steps: Get into your comfortable position: lying, sitting or standing.
Lift and tighten the pelvic floor gently, as if drawing up away from the chair.
Hold for 5 seconds, building toward 10.
Release completely for the same amount of time.
tip: Use about 50% of your maximum squeeze, not 100%.

name: Foundation Quick Pulses (Men)
steps: Lie down or sit.
Squeeze the pelvic floor quickly, then release it right away.
Do 10 in a row, then rest 30 seconds.
tip: Each flick should fully release. If you can't relax between squeezes, slow down.

name: Foundation Elevator Lift (Men)
steps: Imagine the pelvic floor as an elevator rising in 3 floors.
Tighten a little for floor 1, a bit more for floor 2, then more for floor 3.
Hold briefly, then lower one floor at a time until fully relaxed.
tip: Controlled release matters as much as the lift.

name: Bridge with Foundation Lift (Men)
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Exhale, gently lift your pelvic floor, then raise your hips.
Hold 3 seconds at the top, lower down, and fully relax.
tip: Don't arch your lower back. Lift with the glutes.

name: Squat with Foundation Lift (Men)
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
As you stand up from a squat, exhale and gently lift your pelvic floor.
Relax on the way down.
tip: Think of it as a quiet lift, not a hard clench.

name: Foundation Release (Men)
steps: Sit or lie comfortably.
Breathe in and let your pelvic floor drop and widen, as if letting go to pass urine. Do not push or strain.
Breathe out and let the muscles settle.
tip: Helpful if you tend to carry tension in your pelvic area. If you have pelvic pain, check with a clinician first.

name: Foundation Lift Basics (Women)
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Gently tighten as if stopping gas and lifting a blueberry up and in, deep inside.
Hold 3 seconds, then fully relax for 3 seconds.
Do not squeeze your buttocks, thighs or abs, and keep breathing.
tip: Don't practice these while urinating. If you are pregnant, postpartum or have pelvic pain, check with your provider or a pelvic floor physiotherapist.

name: Foundation Endurance Holds (Women)
dose: 10 reps: hold 5–10 seconds, rest equal time
steps: Get into a comfortable position: lying, sitting or standing.
Lift and tighten the pelvic floor gently, up and in.
Hold for 5 seconds, building toward 10.
Release completely for the same amount of time.
tip: Use about 50% of your maximum squeeze, not 100%.

name: Foundation Quick Pulses (Women)
steps: Lie down or sit.
Squeeze the pelvic floor quickly, then release right away.
Do 10 in a row, then rest 30 seconds.
tip: Each flick should fully release.

name: Foundation Elevator Lift (Women)
steps: Imagine the pelvic floor as an elevator rising in 3 floors.
Tighten a little for floor 1, a bit more for floor 2, then more for floor 3.
Hold briefly, then lower one floor at a time until fully relaxed.
tip: Controlled release matters as much as the lift.

name: Bridge with Foundation Lift (Women)
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Exhale, gently lift your pelvic floor, then raise your hips.
Hold 3 seconds at the top, lower down, and fully relax.
tip: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your back.

name: Squat with Foundation Lift (Women)
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
As you stand up from a squat, exhale and gently lift your pelvic floor.
Relax on the way down.
tip: Think of it as a quiet lift, not a hard clench.

name: Foundation Release (Women)
steps: Sit or lie comfortably with knees apart.
Breathe in and allow your pelvic floor to drop and widen. Do not push or strain.
Breathe out and let the muscles settle.
tip: Helpful if you tend to hold tension in the pelvic area. If you have pelvic pain, check with a clinician first.

name: Mountain Pose
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
Press evenly through both feet and lengthen your spine.
Relax your shoulders and breathe slowly.
tip: Use it to reset your posture between other poses.

name: Cat-Cow
steps: Start on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
Inhale, drop your belly and lift your chest and tailbone (cow).
Exhale, round your spine and tuck your chin and tailbone (cat).
tip: Move with your breath. Keep the motion pain-free.

name: Child's Pose
steps: Kneel and sit back toward your heels, knees wide or together.
Fold forward and rest your forehead on the floor with arms reaching out or by your sides.
Breathe into your back.
tip: Place a pillow under your hips or forehead if it feels tight.

name: Downward-Facing Dog
steps: Start on hands and knees, tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back.
Press hands into the floor and lengthen your spine.
Bend your knees as much as needed and relax your head.
tip: Pedal your feet to loosen your calves and hamstrings.

name: Cobra Pose
steps: Lie on your stomach with hands under shoulders.
Press gently into your hands and lift your chest, keeping your hips down.
Keep elbows slightly bent and shoulders away from ears.
tip: Lift with your back muscles, not by pushing hard with your arms.

name: Low Lunge
steps: From hands and knees, step one foot forward between your hands.
Lower the back knee to the floor and sink your hips forward.
Lift your torso and reach arms overhead if comfortable.
tip: Pad your back knee with a folded towel.

name: Warrior I
steps: Step one foot back about a leg's length, back foot turned out 45°.
Bend your front knee over your ankle and square your hips forward.
Reach arms overhead and breathe.
tip: Shorten your stance if your balance is shaky.

name: Warrior II
steps: Step feet wide apart, front toes forward, back foot parallel to the short edge of your mat.
Bend your front knee and extend arms out to the sides.
Gaze over your front hand and keep shoulders over hips.
tip: Keep your front knee tracking over your second toe.

name: Triangle Pose
steps: Stand in a wide stance with front foot forward.
Reach forward with your front hand, then hinge at the hip.
Rest your hand on your shin or a chair, and reach the other arm up.
tip: Use a chair or block for support to keep the chest open.

name: Tree Pose
steps: Stand on one leg and place the other foot on your calf or inner thigh, never on the knee.
Bring hands to your chest or overhead.
Fix your eyes on a still point.
tip: Keep a finger on a wall or counter if you wobble.

name: Chair Pose
steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and sit back as if into a chair.
Reach arms overhead and keep your chest lifted.
tip: Don't let your knees pass your toes.

name: Bridge Pose
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart.
Press into your feet and lift your hips.
Keep your thighs parallel and breathe steadily.
tip: Squeeze your glutes rather than arching your lower back.

name: Seated Forward Fold
steps: Sit with legs straight out in front.
Hinge forward at the hips, keeping your spine long.
Rest your hands on your legs, and stop when you feel a stretch.
tip: Bend your knees or sit on a folded blanket if your hamstrings are tight.

name: Reclined Spinal Twist
steps: Lie on your back with knees pulled in.
Drop your knees to one side and extend your arms out.
Look the opposite way, breathe, then switch.
tip: Place a pillow between your knees if it feels strained.

name: Happy Baby
steps: Lie on your back and bring your knees toward your armpits.
Hold the outsides of your feet or your shins.
Gently rock side to side.
tip: Hold behind the thighs if you can't reach your feet.

name: Legs Up the Wall
steps: Sit sideways next to a wall, then swing your legs up as you lie back.
Rest your arms by your sides, hips near the wall.
Breathe slowly and relax.
tip: Slide your hips farther from the wall if your hamstrings feel tight.

name: Pigeon Pose (Figure-Four Version)
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh.
Pull the lower thigh gently toward your chest.
tip: This is a gentler version of pigeon that is easier on the knees.

name: Sun Salutation Flow
steps: Stand tall, then reach up and fold forward.
Step back to plank, lower down, then rise into cobra.
Press to downward dog, step forward, then stand and reach up.
tip: Link each move to one inhale or exhale and go at your own pace.

name: Boat Pose
steps: Sit with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Lean back slightly and lift your feet until shins are parallel to the floor.
Reach arms forward and keep your chest lifted.
tip: Keep your knees bent or hold the back of your thighs to make it easier.

name: Savasana (Final Rest)
steps: Lie on your back with arms and legs relaxed.
Close your eyes and let your breath return to normal.
Release tension from your face, jaw and shoulders.
tip: Use it to finish a session and let your body absorb the work.

name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Press through your heels and lift your hips.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower.
tip: Place a heavy backpack on your hips for more load later.

name: Wall Sit
steps: Lean back against a wall and slide down until knees are about 90°.
Keep your back flat on the wall and weight in your heels.
Hold and breathe.
tip: Raise your hips a bit if your knees complain.

name: Dead Bug
steps: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent over hips.
Slowly lower your opposite arm and leg toward the floor.
Return and switch sides, keeping your lower back on the floor.
tip: Move slowly. This builds deep core control.

name: Bird Dog
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Hold briefly and return.
tip: Keep your hips level, as if balancing a cup on your lower back.

name: Side Plank
steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so your body forms a line.
Hold, then switch sides.
tip: Bend your bottom knee for an easier version.

name: Superman
steps: Lie face down with arms extended.
Lift arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor.
Pause, then lower slowly.
tip: Look at the floor to keep your neck neutral.

name: Calf Raises
steps: Stand on the edge of a stair or flat ground, holding a rail.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Lower slowly.
tip: Do single-leg raises to progress.

name: Step-Ups
steps: Place one foot fully on the step.
Press through that heel and stand tall.
Step down slowly and repeat.
tip: Hold a backpack for added load.

name: Chair Dips
steps: Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair, hands beside your hips.
Slide forward and lower by bending your elbows to about 90°.
Press back up.
tip: Bend your knees for an easier version. Place the chair against a wall so it can't slide.

name: Incline Push-Up
steps: Place hands on the edge of a counter, body in a straight line.
Lower your chest to the counter.
Press back up.
tip: The higher the surface, the easier it is. Lower the surface to progress.

name: Pike Push-Up
steps: Start in downward dog with hips high.
Bend your elbows and lower your head toward the floor between your hands.
Press back up.
tip: This builds shoulder strength. Stop if your shoulders feel pinched.

name: Backpack Squat
steps: Hold a packed backpack against your chest.
Squat down with your chest up.
Stand back up.
tip: Use a load that you can control for all reps.

name: Backpack Bent-Over Row
steps: Hold the backpack by its handle with one hand and hinge forward.
Pull it toward your hip while keeping your back flat.
Lower slowly. Switch sides.
tip: Rest your other hand on a chair to support your back.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend.
Hinge forward and extend the other leg behind you.
Return to standing by squeezing your glutes.
tip: Touch a chair or wall with a finger for balance.

name: Bicycle Crunch
steps: Lie on your back with hands behind your head.
Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg.
Switch sides in a smooth, controlled pedaling motion.
tip: Slow down and rotate from the ribs, not by pulling on your neck.

name: Hollow Hold
steps: Lie on your back and press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your shoulders and legs a few inches off the floor.
Hold and breathe.
tip: Bend your knees or raise your legs higher to make it easier.

name: Reverse Crunch
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent over hips.
Curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Lower slowly.
tip: Avoid swinging with momentum.

name: Split Squat with Back Foot on Couch
steps: Stand facing away from a couch and place one foot on the cushion behind you.
Lower your back knee toward the floor.
Press through the front foot to stand.
tip: Hold a backpack for added load. Keep the front knee over the ankle.

name: Water Jug Farmer Carry
equipment: Two filled water jugs or bags
steps: Hold a jug or loaded bag in each hand with arms at your sides.
Stand tall and walk steadily.
Set the jugs down carefully.
tip: Choose loads you can carry with good posture and a firm grip.

name: Neck Half-Circles
steps: Sit or stand tall.
Slowly tilt your ear toward your shoulder, then roll your chin down across your chest to the other side.
Avoid tipping your head back.
tip: Keep it gentle and pain-free.

name: Shoulder Rolls
steps: Stand tall with arms relaxed.
Draw big circles with your shoulders.
Switch directions.
tip: Roll slowly and breathe.

name: Thread the Needle
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Slide one arm under your chest, palm up.
Rest your shoulder and ear on the floor, then return.
tip: Move slowly to stretch the upper back and shoulders.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward.
Tuck your tailbone and shift your hips forward.
Reach the same arm as the back knee overhead.
tip: Pad your knee with a folded towel.

name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
steps: Place one heel on a low step or chair, leg straight.
Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the back of your thigh.
tip: Don't round your back to reach further.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
steps: Place your forearms on both sides of a doorframe.
Step one foot forward and lean gently.
Feel the stretch across your chest.
tip: Keep your ribs down and shoulders relaxed.

name: 90/90 Hip Switches
steps: Sit with both knees bent at 90° and rotated to the same side.
Lift your knees and rotate them to the other side.
Keep your torso tall.
tip: Place your hands behind you for support.

name: Ankle Circles
steps: Sit and lift one foot off the floor.
Draw slow circles with your toes.
Switch directions, then switch feet.
tip: Do these any time your ankles feel stiff.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
steps: From a plank, step one foot beside your hand.
Rotate your chest and reach the inside arm to the ceiling.
Return, then switch sides.
tip: Go slow and breathe into the stretch.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
steps: Bring one arm across your chest.
Use the other hand to hold it gently in place.
Keep your shoulders relaxed.
tip: Don't pull on the elbow joint.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
steps: Hold a wall for balance.
Bend one knee and hold your ankle behind you.
Keep your knees close and hips level.
tip: Squeeze the glute of the stretched leg.

name: Wrist Circles and Stretches
steps: Make circles with your wrists.
Extend one arm with your palm up and gently pull your fingers back.
Repeat with your palm down.
tip: Great after long periods at a keyboard.

name: March in Place
steps: Stand tall and lift your knees alternately.
Swing your arms.
Keep a steady rhythm.
tip: A great warm-up or low-impact option.

name: Jumping Jacks
steps: Stand with feet together and arms down.
Jump your feet wide as your arms rise overhead.
Jump back to the start.
tip: Step side to side instead of jumping for low impact.

name: High Knees
steps: Run in place, lifting your knees to hip height.
Pump your arms.
Land softly.
tip: Slow down to a march if you need to.

name: Shadow Boxing
steps: Stand with a staggered stance, fists up.
Throw jabs and crosses at the air.
Stay light on your feet.
tip: Add footwork and slips as you get comfortable.

name: Skater Hops
steps: Hop sideways from one leg to the other.
Swing your arms and let your back foot trail behind.
Land softly with a slight knee bend.
tip: Step instead of hop for a gentler version.

name: Stair Climbing
steps: Walk or jog up a flight of stairs at a steady pace.
Walk down carefully.
Repeat for the time.
tip: Use the handrail and wear supportive shoes.

name: Squat Jumps
steps: Squat down, then explode upward into a jump.
Land softly, bending your knees.
Immediately squat again.
tip: Skip this if you have knee or ankle problems.

name: Step Jacks
steps: Step one foot out to the side while raising your arms.
Step it back and repeat on the other side.
Keep moving at a steady rhythm.
tip: A low-impact jumping-jack alternative.

name: Butt Kicks
steps: Jog in place.
Kick your heels toward your glutes.
Keep your posture tall.
tip: Good warm-up for your hamstrings.

name: Imaginary Jump Rope
steps: Hop lightly on the balls of your feet.
Circle your wrists as if turning a rope.
Keep your jumps small.
tip: Alternate feet to reduce impact.

name: Living Room Dance Break
steps: Put on an upbeat song.
Move however you like.
Keep your heart rate up for the whole track.
tip: The best workout is the one you enjoy.

name: Decline Push-Up (Feet on Chair)
steps: Place your feet on a sturdy chair or low couch arm and hands on the floor.
Keep your body in one line and lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up without letting your hips sag.
tip: Builds the upper chest and shoulders. Make sure the chair can't slide.

name: Archer Push-Up
steps: Start in a wide push-up position.
Lower toward one hand while the other arm stays straight.
Press back up and switch sides.
tip: Work up to this from regular push-ups. Keep the straight arm's elbow soft.

name: Backpack Curl
steps: Stand holding the backpack by its handle, arm at your side.
Bend your elbow to lift it toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still.
Lower slowly. Switch arms.
tip: Choose a load you can lift for all reps without swinging.

name: Backpack Overhead Press
steps: Hold a packed backpack at chest height with both hands.
Brace your core and press it overhead.
Lower under control.
tip: Keep ribs down and avoid leaning back.

name: Prone Y-T-W Raises
steps: Lie face down with arms in a Y shape and lift them a few inches.
Lower, then repeat with arms out like a T, then bent in a W.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together each time.
tip: Great for posture and the muscles that support your shoulders.

name: Donkey Kick
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Keeping your knee bent at 90°, press your heel toward the ceiling.
Squeeze the glute at the top, lower, and repeat.
tip: Keep your hips level and avoid arching your lower back.

name: Fire Hydrant
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Lift one knee out to the side, keeping the knee bent.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tip: Move from the hip, not by twisting your back.

name: Sumo Squat
steps: Stand with feet wider than your shoulders, toes turned out.
Bend your knees and lower your hips straight down.
Press through your heels and squeeze your glutes at the top.
tip: Hold a backpack at your chest to add load later.

name: Curtsy Lunge
steps: Stand tall, then step one foot back and across behind the other.
Lower both knees, keeping the front knee over your ankle.
Return to standing and switch sides.
tip: Hold a counter for balance at first.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent. Extend one leg straight.
Press through the other heel and lift your hips.
Lower slowly. Switch legs.
tip: Keep your hips level. Don't let one side drop.

name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
steps: Lie on your side with legs stacked and bottom knee bent.
Lift your top leg a little behind your body's centerline.
Lower slowly.
tip: Squeeze the side of your hip. Don't roll backward.

name: Heel Drops
steps: Stand tall and rise onto your toes.
Let your heels drop to the floor with a firm but controlled thump.
Repeat. Hold a counter if needed.
tip: A gentle impact exercise that supports bone health. Skip if you have foot, ankle or balance problems.

name: Single-Leg Balance
steps: Stand tall near a counter and lift one foot a few inches.
Keep your hips level and eyes on a fixed point.
Hold, then switch legs.
tip: Progress by closing your eyes or standing on a folded towel.

name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
steps: Place the heel of one foot directly in front of the toes of the other.
Walk in a straight line with arms out for balance.
Look ahead, not down.
tip: Use a wall for support if you need it.

name: Wall Angels
steps: Stand with your back, head and hips lightly against a wall.
Raise your arms to the sides in a goalpost shape.
Slide them up and down the wall without arching your back.
tip: Stop short of any pinching in your shoulders.

name: Chin Tucks
steps: Sit or stand tall.
Gently glide your chin straight back as if making a double chin.
Hold, then relax.
tip: Great to counter long hours looking at a screen.

name: Posture Reset
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Roll your shoulders back and down, lengthen the crown of your head toward the ceiling.
Take 3 slow breaths.
tip: Set a reminder to do this a few times a day.

name: Box Breathing
steps: Breathe in through your nose for 4 counts.
Hold for 4. Breathe out for 4. Hold for 4.
Repeat, keeping your shoulders relaxed.
tip: Shorten the counts to 3 if 4 feels strained.

name: 4-7-8 Calming Breath
steps: Breathe in quietly through your nose for 4 counts.
Hold for 7.
Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 8.
tip: Stop if you feel lightheaded. Gentle breathing is enough.

name: Body Scan
steps: Lie down and close your eyes.
Move your attention slowly from your toes to the top of your head.
Notice each area without trying to change it.
tip: If your mind wanders, gently return to the area you were on.

name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
steps: Tense one muscle group (feet, calves, thighs, hands, arms, shoulders, face) for 5 seconds.
Release suddenly and notice the relaxation for 10 seconds.
Move up through your body.
tip: Tense gently, about 60% effort. Never to the point of pain.

name: Mindful Walking
steps: Walk slowly, noticing the feeling of each footstep.
Notice sounds, air on your skin and your breathing.
When your mind drifts, return to your steps.
tip: Works indoors or out, with no phone.

name: Three Good Things
steps: Sit quietly and think of three good things from your day, however small.
For each one, think about why it happened or what it means to you.
Write them down or say them aloud.
tip: A simple habit that supports mood and sleep.

name: Loving-Kindness Minute
steps: Sit comfortably and breathe slowly.
Silently say: 'May I be well. May I be safe. May I be kind to myself.'
Repeat for a friend, then for someone you find difficult.
tip: Be patient. The feeling is less important than the intention.

name: Shake It Out
steps: Stand and shake your hands, arms, then legs loosely.
Add your shoulders and torso, then your whole body.
Finish with 3 deep breaths.
tip: A quick way to release stress and reset.

name: Gratitude Stretch
steps: Reach your arms overhead and breathe in.
As you lower them, think of one thing you're grateful for.
Repeat 5 times with a different thought each time.
tip: Pairs naturally with your morning routine.

name: Five Senses Grounding
steps: Name 5 things you can see, 4 you can feel, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell and 1 you can taste.
Breathe slowly between each group.
tip: Helpful when your mind is racing.

name: Slow Exhale Reset
steps: Breathe in through your nose for 4 counts.
Breathe out slowly through pursed lips for 6–8 counts.
Repeat for 10 breaths.
tip: A longer exhale helps your body settle.

name: Dead Hang
steps: Grip the bar with palms facing away, hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Hang with arms straight and shoulders relaxed, feet off the floor or lightly supported.
Breathe steadily and hold.
tip: Builds grip and shoulder health. Use a chair under your feet if you can't hang fully yet.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
steps: Hang from the bar with straight arms.
Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and back to lift your body a couple of inches.
Lower slowly back to a full hang.
tip: A small move that teaches your back to start the pull.

name: Australian Row (Under a Table)
steps: Lie under a very sturdy table and grip its edge with both hands, arms straight.
Keep your body in one straight line with heels on the floor.
Pull your chest up toward your hands, then lower slowly.
tip: Bend your knees to make it easier. Only use a table that can't tip or slide.

name: Negative Pull-Up
steps: Step or jump up so your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself as slowly as you can, aiming for 3–5 seconds.
Return to the start with a step, not a drop.
tip: The best way to build up to your first full pull-up.

name: Chin-Up
steps: Grip the bar with palms facing you, hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull until your chin is over the bar, elbows close to your sides.
Lower under control to straight arms.
tip: Usually a little easier than a pull-up because your biceps help more.

name: Pull-Up
steps: Grip the bar with palms facing away, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Start from a full hang, brace your core and pull your chest toward the bar.
Get your chin over the bar, then lower under control to straight arms.
tip: Can't do one yet? Start with Dead Hangs, Scapular Pull-Ups and Negative Pull-Ups. Make sure a doorway bar is rated for your weight.
